whatItDoes: A decentralized 'outsourcing intelligence' platform: customers define measurable competitions (task + data + scoring function) and a global pool of human and agentic-AI solvers competes to solve them. Validators score submissions in isolated sandboxes and emissions flow winner-takes-all to the top-ranked solver. Used for autoresearch, algorithm discovery, RL training and data engineering.
hardwareRec: No fixed GPU floor in repo — compute is competition-dependent (often CPU + LLM-agent workflows; some competitions may want GPUs). Budget mostly for research time and per-competition submission fees, not always hardware.
keyRequirements: Apex CLI installed from repo (uv workspace)
Bittensor wallet linked via `apex link`
Per-competition submission fee (varies, listed in docs)
Solution must match the competition's file format
Top leaderboard rank at payout time wins
Agentic mining guide: repo AGENTS.md
minerJob: Miners are 'solvers': pick an active competition, fork the baseline in shared/competition/, and iterate on a solution maximizing the objective f(x)→R. Submissions go through the Apex CLI, which signs, charges the entry fee and uploads; validators run each submission in an isolated sandbox against the customer's scoring function and keep leaderboards continuously updated. Rewards are winner-takes-all per competition — the top-ranked submission earns that competition's emissions on-chain, shifting as the leaderboard changes. Solutions are community-shared, so progress compounds.
minerJobProvide: Competition solutions (code/models) scoring best on f(x)
Per-competition submissions in the required format
Iterated improvements beating other solvers' leaders
top10Strategy: Treat each competition as a short research sprint: read the per-competition spec, fork the baseline, and spend budget only where expected score gain is largest — winner-takes-all makes 'pretty good' worthless. Study shared solutions and compound on the community's best ideas. Pick competitions matching your edge rather than entering everything; a fee is sunk cost unless you can plausibly reach rank 1.
top10Levers: Pick competitions matching your team's edge
Fork and improve the repo baseline solution
Agentic loops (LLM researchers) to widen search
Fee discipline: enter only when rank-1 is plausible
Understand scoring quirks and sandbox constraints
followTopMiners: Watch the docs.macrocosmos.ai current-competitions page and `apex list -c <id> -t` leaderboards; track taostats.io/subnet/1 weight shifts per competition; join the Macrocosmos Discord #apex; monitor repo commits and AGENTS.md updates.

whatItDoes: A settlement layer for AI agents: an agent holding SOL, TAO, BTC or another supported asset submits one swap and receives the destination asset natively in its own wallet — no bridges, wrapped tokens or custodian. Miners are market makers: they post quotes, lock collateral and fulfill swaps; validators verify both legs on-chain and slash collateral on failure.
hardwareRec: CPU only (any small VPS runs it via Docker Compose). The real input is capital: SOL or TAO collateral bonds, funded delivery wallets per chain (BTC/ETH/etc.), plus a one-time 0.1 SOL identity deposit for hotkey binding.
keyRequirements: Python 3.10+, Docker Compose miner stack
Bittensor wallet; .env with PORT/WALLET_PATH
Collateral bond (SOL purse or locked TAO vault bond)
Private keys per delivery chain (BTC, ETH, ...)
alw miner bind-hotkey + activate before quoting
Failed deliveries are slashed from your collateral
minerJob: Run the reference miner container and quote lanes (e.g. SOL↔TAO) with `alw miner post`. When a taker reserves your quote, you deliver the destination asset to their wallet within the swap window; validators attest both legs on-chain and your credibility accrues from completed swaps. The optional Quote Optimizer auto-reprices 0.4% under the best competing quote inside the validators' 0.5% crown band, pulls quotes when wallets can't cover a full fill, and reports strikes via Discord webhooks.
top10Strategy: This is a market-making business, not a compute one: earnings come from being the best quote on active lanes while never missing a fill. Undercut rivals inside the 0.5% crown band, keep delivery wallets funded for full-size fills (a missed fill costs a 10% premium strike), and tune the optimizer's per-lane tolerances. More collateral → bigger fill capacity → more weight; strikes and timeouts destroy both TAO and standing.
top10Levers: Tightest quotes within the 0.5% crown band
Quote Optimizer with tuned lane tolerances
Multi-lane coverage incl. opt-in BTC lanes
Zero missed fills / no timeout strikes
Funded BTC fee reserves on BTC lanes
followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/7 top-UID dividends, docs.all-ways.io updates and the @allways_io X account; watch your own webhook strike/fee alerts and the public API (api.all-ways.io) quote book to see which hotkeys lead each lane.

whatItDoes: Macrocosmos's data-scraping and sentiment subnet: miners scrape real-time X (Twitter), Reddit and YouTube-transcript data, store it locally, and expose it to validators that power products like Gravity (no-code scraping), Nebula (visualization) and the Macrocosmos API/MCP. Businesses and other subnets buy this data; miners earn for holding fresh, desirable, non-duplicated data.
hardwareRec: CPU only — no GPU needed. Prioritize cores for scraping throughput, large fast storage/databases for DataEntities, and bandwidth. S3-compatible storage setup required for public dataset upload.

Data must be <30 days old to score

Respect source ToS; anonymized data only
minerJob: Day-to-day the miner scrapes configured DataSources (X, Reddit, YouTube transcripts), files each DataEntity into buckets (source, time bucket, label) forming its MinerIndex, and answers validator queries for that index. Validators sample and verify items to build a credibility score, then weight miners by data value: freshness (<30 days), position on the Dynamic Desirability List (driven by Gravity user requests), and a duplication factor that pays a premium for data few others hold. Miners also upload anonymized copies to S3 for public dataset access.

top10Strategy: Win by differentiation, not volume: use the hosted sn13-dashboard to find buckets where desirability is high but few miners hold data, since duplication directly divides value. Keep everything under 30 days old, refresh continuously, and never inflate your index — credibility sampling punishes misrepresentation harder than honest smallness. React fast when the Desirability List changes (updates are announced ahead of time).

whatItDoes: A video-understanding benchmark subnet: miners submit immutable video-language model weights; evaluator validators privately test them on random audiovisual clips from a 1,000-video catalogue and crown one 'king' per window. 100% of each validator's weight goes to that single king (0% burn otherwise) — a winner-take-all leaderboard for multimodal video models.
hardwareRec: Miner needs no GPU to serve — a CPU server distributes weights (packages up to 24–44 GB). GPU spend goes into training/selecting a model strong enough to beat the king; A100/H100-class for experimentation.

Full safetensors weights (no adapters), size-capped
One hotkey binds one model permanently
CPU model server on public IP (default port 8091)
Pinned TLS + btauth/1 signed requests; zstd ranges
Downloaders must hold ≥100,000 SN20 alpha
minerJob: Run `witness-benchmark-miner prepare` to hash the package and mint a TLS certificate, `serve` to host weights over authenticated TLS (HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, 4 MiB ranges, zstd), and `commit` to publish the wm2 manifest+cert commitment on-chain. Evaluators download the weights, run the model on private video clips with validator-owned loaders, and score quality/reward/paired-king metrics; the miner never serves inference. Your model stays king only while challengers fail to beat its paired reward by more than 0.02.

top10Strategy: King-of-the-hill: study the reigning king's published scores and only enter a model you believe clears the +0.02 paired-improvement margin with aggregate quality >0.05 — a terminal evaluation consumes the hotkey for that evaluator, and one hotkey binds one model forever. Serve from a fast, stable endpoint: slow downloads (15-minute acquisition cap) are dropped without scoring. New submissions queue for the next two-epoch window.

Endpoint availability so retries keep queue spot
followTopMiners: Track the witness dashboard (queue, kings, per-window scores), taostats.io/subnet/20 weight concentration on the single king, repo commit cadence (evaluation-v3, window policy changes), and witnessvision.io announcements.

whatItDoes: A decentralized adversarial-robustness network. Validators publish an ImageNet-1k image every two minutes; miners must find an imperceptible perturbation that flips EfficientNetV2-L's prediction. Outputs feed a growing adversarial-training dataset and on-chain robustness certificates (relevant to EU AI Act conformity) for enterprise and safety customers.
hardwareRec: Miner: 8 vCPU / 32 GB RAM with any 8+ GB NVIDIA GPU (12–24 GB comfortable); attack search speed matters more than VRAM. Optional model track (fine-tuning EfficientNetV2-L) wants a bigger GPU. No axon exposure needed; rentals fine.
keyRequirements: Python 3.10+, Node 18+/PM2, scripts/run_miner.sh
Miner env: WALLET_NAME/HOTKEY, NETUID, NETWORK
Registered hotkey; no axon exposure required
Submissions: image URL + sha256 pixel hash
Hard gates: L∞ bounds, SSIM, PSNR, label flip
Model track: on-chain commitment sha256(model||hotkey)
minerJob: Poll the task API for the current ImageNet-1k image, run your attack (baseline is PGD) to find a perturbation within L∞/SSIM/PSNR limits that flips the classifier, then upload the image and submit its URL plus pixel hash. Validators recompute hashes and score: smaller, subtler perturbations score higher ((1−ratio)² terms plus small margin/novelty bonuses). Scanning emissions split 75/20/5 across the top three ranks; separately, a daily adversarially-trained EfficientNetV2-L contest pays 20% of miner emissions to the day's winner. Weights come from stake-weighted cross-validator leaderboard ranks.
minerJobProvide: Compliant perturbations passing all hard gates
Stable image URLs with matching pixel hashes
top10Strategy: Emissions are brutally top-heavy — rank 1 takes 75% of the 80% scanning pot — so optimize attack quality: minimize L∞/RMSE ratios while staying under epsilon and above SSIM/PSNR floors, and poll fast enough to never miss a task. Beating the baseline PGD (better initialization, momentum, adaptive steps) is the core lever. Note avgScore needs a ~50-record history before it counts. The daily model track is a separate lottery — enter only with a genuinely strong fine-tune.
top10Levers: Stronger attack optimizer than baseline PGD
Consistency: top-3 on every validator's leaderboard
followTopMiners: Watch the public leaderboard reports (per-validator avgScore), taostats.io/subnet/26 for the 75/20/5 weight pattern, repo commits for scoring-constant changes (PERTURB_* envs), and the perturbai.io whitepaper/Discord.

whatItDoes: A GAN-style competition for synthetic-media detection. Discriminative miners submit image/video/audio deepfake-detection classifiers; generative miners run servers producing synthetic media on demand; validators benchmark both. Detectors improve as fakes improve. Products serve provenance/detection APIs; app.bitmind.ai tracks the reigning kings per modality.
hardwareRec: Discriminative track: no GPU hosting — upload safetensors classifiers (the A100/80 GB input spec reflects the generative track). Generative track: GPU inference server (A100-class) producing image+video at volume. Detector miners can run anywhere.

Generators must clear fool-rate gate (img>2%, vid>1%)

Submission allowances shared across modalities
minerJob: Detectors: train a media-provenance classifier, zip and push via gascli; validators score it (sn34_score = MCC + Brier error) on public, private-holdout and fresh GAS-Station data across three modalities. Each lane has a king (image 40%, video 40%, audio 4% of miner emissions) split 85/10/5 across the current and two previous kings; dethrone by +0.01 sn34_score on the same benchmark version. Generators: answer validator prompts with verified synthetic media; the 16% generator pot pays per verified volume × √(price/baseline) × pass-rate, only in modalities that clear the 7-day fool-rate gate.
top10Strategy: Detector lanes are king-of-the-hill with 85/10/5 memory — beating a king by just 0.01 takes the lane, so track each lane's sn34_score and target the weakest modality (audio is only 4%). Prioritize calibration (Brier) as much as accuracy, and retrain weekly against refreshed GAS-Station fakes. For generators, clearing the fool-rate gate is binary; after that, verified volume and the model price multiplier drive payout.
top10Levers: Generation volume with strong price multiplier
Robustness to the augmentation blend in scoring
followTopMiners: Track app.bitmind.ai leaderboard kings per modality, `gascli d perf` for your benchmark scores, taostats.io/subnet/34 dividend concentration, the BitMind Discord for round-config changes, and docs/Incentive.md updates.

whatItDoes: A decentralized network for graph optimization, currently focused on the Traveling Salesman Problem. Validators send synthetic TSP instances; miners return tours scored against the best cohort solution and a greedy benchmark. Aimed at logistics/routing use cases; a planned frontend will let users submit their own graph problems.
hardwareRec: CPU only — TSP quality is algorithm work, not GPU work. The repo ships four starter algorithms (Nearest Neighbour, Dynamic Programming, Beam Search, Hybrid Pointer Network); custom high-performance solvers are the differentiator.
keyRequirements: Python miner per docs/miner.md
Respond with tours within the required timeframe
Support coordinate (undirected) and edge (directed) inputs
Beat the greedy benchmark or be penalized
Team warns of breaking changes — join Discord
minerJob: Run the miner neuron from the Graphite repo; validators broadcast TSP instances and the miner returns high-quality tours computed by its solver. Scoring compares your tour length relative to the best solution in the cohort and a benchmark greedy heuristic; solutions falling short of the benchmark are penalized. Upgrading from the bundled heuristics to stronger solvers (better local search, or improved learned approaches like the provided pointer network) is how weight share is won.
minerJobProvide: Custom solver improvements over bundled algorithms
top10Strategy: This is an algorithms race: the bundled algorithms are the floor, not the ceiling — winners implement stronger TSP solvers (OR-tools/LKH-style local search or improved learned models) that reliably beat the greedy benchmark by a wide margin at low latency. Because scoring is relative to the cohort, small consistent margins across every instance compound into a dominant weight share.
top10Levers: Stronger custom TSP solver than baselines
Wide margin over the greedy benchmark
followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/43 top UIDs and weight spread, the Graphite Discord for scoring/algorithm updates (team warns of breaking changes), and commit cadence on GraphiteAI/Graphite-Subnet.

Validators broadcast dataset-generation tasks; miners produce lists of experiments (guide RNAs, targets, mutations, Cas systems, cell types) which validators score through a five-stage biological validation pipeline. Output feeds genome-editing ML research.
hardwareRec: Repo lists no GPU requirement — the workload is structured data generation (CPU; LLM-assisted generation plausible). Input metadata flags 'GPU required, model/VRAM unspecified' — confirm with the team before renting GPUs.

minerJob: Receive the CRISPR task spec from validators, generate a diverse list of biologically plausible experiments conforming to the contract (20–23bp guideRNAs, PAM-valid targets, whitelisted HBB mutations like HbS, Cas9/Cas12a, approved cell types), and upload the dataset to the validator's S3 bucket. Validators alone compute biological outcomes through five progressive stages (syntax, statistical plausibility, biophysical simulation, cross-consistency ML, distributional fidelity to real CRISPR data) and weight miners by multi-stage scores. Validation constraints tighten over time — adapt fast when stages evolve.

whatItDoes: A verified media-placement subnet: PR firms and contributors publish editorial articles in real news outlets against briefs. Validators run a code-only verification oracle checking each article on the outlet's own page (signed registry, brief window, topic match, not-paid-content, text match) and weight the contributor's hotkey by verified USD value; uncovered emission burns.
hardwareRec: CPU only — in fact no miner server at all. The real 'hardware' is PR placement: you need real outlets willing to publish on-brief editorial content. Hotkey is registered through the Herald website with a wallet extension.

Validators orchestrate the training loop — routing activations to experts, collecting updated weights/gradients, aggregating — and score miners on contribution quality and reliability, setting weights each epoch. whatItDoes: An incentive network for training-data improvement: miners generate bounded synthetic or licensed data patches (initially math and natural sciences) with record-level provenance; validators verify rights, privacy, lineage and contamination, then train a frozen baseline with each patch and reward measured capability improvements. Quality gains — not dataset size or compute — earn TAO.
hardwareRec: No GPU requirement stated in the repo. Patch generation likely leans on LLM API budgets rather than local GPUs; the train-and-evaluate comparisons run validator-side under identical conditions.
keyRequirements: Bounded data patches with record-level provenance
Appropriate usage rights mandatory (no unlicensed material)
No private info or real-minor data
Pass contamination/leakage/duplication checks
Patches tested against a frozen baseline
Objective subjects first: math + natural sciences
minerJob: Produce candidate data patches — synthetic or licensed examples with answers, reasoning steps, calculations and explanations for learning-oriented tasks — carrying provenance metadata per record. Validators run a GENERATE → VERIFY → TRAIN → EVALUATE → REWARD pipeline: they check rights, privacy, lineage, duplication and evaluation leakage, then fine-tune a frozen baseline with your patch under identical training and evaluation conditions. Rewards are proportional to measurable improvements in factual accuracy, reasoning quality, calibration, clear age-appropriate communication and safety without unnecessary refusal.
top10Strategy: It's an A/B-test economy: your patch must beat the frozen baseline under identical training conditions, so prioritize data that moves measurable metrics — worked examples with correct steps and units, calibration pairs, safety-without-refusal cases — over bulk. Contamination or evaluation leakage disqualifies a patch; verify uniqueness before submitting. Start with narrow, objectively-checkable domains where you can demonstrably lift accuracy.
top10Levers: Patches that measurably lift baseline accuracy
followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/119 top UIDs, repo commit cadence for evaluation-standard updates (scope expands only as reliable evaluation standards arrive), and any published baseline/evaluation changes before crafting patches.

whatItDoes: An incentivized ML-research network: miners submit optimizer code; validators train a ~360M Llama-style model with it under a fixed B200 budget (≤20 h, FineWeb-Edu) and score validation loss. Confirmed improvements beyond an adaptive bar (floor 0.03 nats) earn credit with a 14-day half-life. First research target: better gradient descent.
hardwareRec: No GPU needed merely to serve a submission — the validator's B200 runs scored runs (B200 is the only SKU allowed to score; 180 GB VRAM class). Real research requires your own training compute (A100/H100-class realistic).

minerJob: Implement an optimizer in Python against the template interface, test it against matched controls on your own compute, then serve its source from your miner hotkey and fund evaluation credits for the round. Validators verify the committed source hash, run the scored training contract (360M model, seq 2,048, batch 32, ≤188k steps on one B200), and confirm promising candidates with a second validator-funded run. Credit scales with improvement size and decays with a 14-day half-life; rewards are shared by credit weight and unearned emission burns.
top10Strategy: Pure research competition: study the signed round contract before spending (historical reference numbers are not live targets), and only submit candidates that clear the adaptive improvement bar in your own matched-control tests — failed paid evaluations are pure loss. Compounding wins matter: confirmed optimizers become the frontier others must beat, so iteration speed on the learning-rate-schedule/update-rule search space (including LLM research agents) is the real edge.
